claims.text: Volvo EX30 boot/cargo capacity (EU measurement): ~318 litres with rear seats up and ~904 litres with the rear seats folded; a small front trunk (frunk) of roughly 7 litres is also reported.
Multiple European reviews report the EX30’s boot as about 318–400 litres with seats up and 904 litres seats down (example: CompleteCar.ie shows 318–400 L / 904 L).

Several owner posts and EX30-owner forums report front-seat firmness or a lack of lateral/leg support for some drivers (owners reporting they found the seats initially uncomfortable or lacking side support).
claims.about: Volvo EX30 owner seat comfort reports

claims.text: Professional reviews are mixed but often positive about EX30 front seats: AutoCar and AutoTrader note the EX30’s front seats as “broad and comfy” or “very comfortable” in their road tests.
BMW 1 Series (F70, 2024/2025 EU model) official/spec figures: standard luggage capacity 380 litres (some mild‑hybrid 120/120d versions 300 litres), expanding to 1,200 litres with rear seats folded.
BMW reviews (Auto Express and others) describe the 1 Series’ front seats as supportive and comfortable for long journeys, with good adjustability; some sporty seat options are available as extras.
claims.about: BMW 1 Series front seat comfort (Auto Express)

claims.text: Rear‑seat space comparison from published reviews: EX30 rear-seat legroom is repeatedly described as ‘tight’ for taller adults, while the BMW 1 Series is described as ‘reasonable’ but still somewhat cramped—overall the 1 Series generally offers more rear passenger room than the EX30 in reviewer tests.
claims.about: Volvo EX30 rear seat space (JD Power)

claims.text: Cabin storage/practicality: reviewers note the EX30 has useful small storage (front cubby, under‑floor boot storage, pockets) but smaller door bins and tighter rear passenger storage; the BMW 1 Series’ cabin storage is described as ‘average’ with a central armrest bin and cupholders—practical differences are small but the BMW’s larger boot makes it more practical for bulk luggage.

Bottom-line, EU 2025/2026: Volvo EX30 is a compact, well‑designed small electric SUV with a usable but modest 318 L boot (904 L folded) and mixed front-seat feedback (some reviewers praise comfort; some owners report lack of lateral/under‑thigh support), whereas the BMW 1 Series (F70) typically offers a larger standard boot (≈380 L depending on variant), more rear‑seat room in many trims and generally receives stronger comments about front-seat support—so BMW tends to be better for bulk luggage and rear‑seat space, while the EX30 focuses on a compact EV packaging and minimalist interior.
claims.publisher: Synthesis of above sources (examples: Recharged, BMW press, Auto Express, RAC, owner forums)
claims.about: Comparison summary EX30 vs BMW 1 Series (F70)
